1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	Metaformalism Copilot is a Next.js web app for transforming insights and source material into personalized, context-sensitive formalisms. It's part of the [Live Conversational Threads](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/uueHkKrGmeEsKGHPR/live-conversational-threads-not-an-ai-notetaker-2) research project. The philosophy ("Live Theory") emphasizes generalization via inclusion — producing multiple rigorous representations tailored to specific contexts rather than a single unified theory.
8	
9	## Prerequisites
10	
11	- Node.js (v18+) and npm
12	- An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable for LLM features
13	
14	## Commands
15	
16	All commands run from the repo root:
17	
18	```bash
19	npm run dev        # Start dev server at localhost:3000
20	npm run build      # Production build
21	npm run lint       # ESLint (eslint-config-next with core-web-vitals + typescript)
22	npm test           # Run tests (Vitest)
23	npm run test:watch # Run tests in watch mode
24	npm run test:ui    # Run tests with Vitest UI
25	```
26	
27	## Architecture
28	
29	The app is a **multi-panel workspace** with a collapsible Icon Rail sidebar for navigation. The root `page.tsx` orchestrates all state and renders the active panel via a `PanelShell` layout. State is persisted to localStorage via `useWorkspacePersistence` and survives page refreshes.
30	
31	### Directory Layout (under `app/`)
32	
33	- `page.tsx` — Root orchestrator: manages panel navigation, all workspace state, and delegates to panel components
34	- `layout.tsx` — Sets up fonts (EB Garamond serif + Geist Mono) and metadata
35	- `globals.css` — CSS variables (`--ivory-cream`, `--ink-black`, `--paper-shadow`) and Tailwind v4 config via `@theme inline`
36	- `components/layout/` — `PanelShell` (Icon Rail + focus pane layout), `IconRail` (sidebar navigation)
37	- `components/panels/` — One component per panel: `InputPanel`, `SemiformalPanel`, `LeanPanel`, `GraphPanel`, `NodeDetailPanel`, `CausalGraphPanel`, `StatisticalModelPanel`, `PropertyTestsPanel`, `DialecticalMapPanel`, `AnalyticsPanel`
38	- `components/features/` — Feature modules organized by domain:
39	  - `source-input/` — `TextInput`, `FileUpload` (.txt, .doc, .docx, .pdf)
40	  - `context-input/` — `ContextInput`, `RefinementButtons`, `RefinementPreview`
41	  - `output-editing/` — `EditableOutput`; `ai-bars/InlineEditPopup` (Cmd+K) and `ai-bars/WholeTextEditBar`
42	  - `workspace-session/` — `WorkspaceSessionBar` for session switching
43	  - `session-banner/` — `SessionBanner` for per-panel session context
44	  - `artifact-selector/` — Artifact type selection UI
45	  - `causal-graph/` — Graph visualization components
46	  - `lean-display/` — Lean code display with syntax highlighting
47	- `components/ui/` — Shared UI components and icons
48	- `hooks/` — Custom hooks: `useWorkspacePersistence`, `useWorkspaceSessions`, `useFormalizationPipeline`, `useDecomposition`, `useAutoFormalizeQueue`, `useAnalytics`, etc.
49	- `lib/types/` — TypeScript type definitions for panels, sessions, artifacts, decomposition
50	- `lib/llm/` — LLM integration (Anthropic SDK, schemas, caching)
51	- `lib/formalization/` — Shared artifact generation logic
52	- `lib/utils/` — Utilities (PDF parsing, LaTeX parsing, export, text selection)
53	- `api/` — Next.js API routes for formalization, editing, verification, decomposition, analytics
54	
55	### Key Patterns
56	
57	- **Feature-based folder structure**: components grouped by feature domain, not by type
58	- **Import alias**: `@/*` maps to the project root (configured in `tsconfig.json`)
59	- **Client components**: Panel components use `"use client"` since they manage state
60	- **Multiple artifact types**: semiformal, lean, causal-graph, statistical-model, property-tests, dialectical-map — each with a dedicated panel and API route
61	- **Decomposition workflow**: extract propositions from sources into a dependency graph, then formalize per-node
62	- **Session management**: workspace sessions (global) and formalization sessions (per-scope) for tracking artifact history
63	
64	### Design System
65	
66	- CSS variables in `globals.css` are the source of truth for theming
67	- Tailwind CSS v4 with `@tailwindcss/postcss`
68	- Primary font: EB Garamond (serif); Mono: Geist Mono
69	- Styling uses both Tailwind classes and `var(--css-variable)` references
70	
71	## Code Guidelines
72	
73	- TypeScript for all components
74	- Tailwind CSS for styling; theme colors via CSS variables in `globals.css`
75	- Components should be modular and single-responsibility
76	- Follow existing feature-based folder structure in `app/components/features/`
77	- Ensure `npm run lint` passes before committing
78	
79	## Git Workflow
80	
81	- Always work on feature branches, never commit directly to main
82	- Commit after each logical unit of work with conventional commit messages (feat:, fix:, refactor:, test:, docs:)
83	- Push the branch after each commit so work is backed up remotely
84	- Before finishing a session, ensure all work is committed and pushed
85	- When asked to prepare for review, do an interactive rebase to clean up WIP commits into logical chunks
86	
87	## Code Quality
88	
89	- Tests use Vitest with React Testing Library. Write tests alongside implementation.
90	- Add comments explaining "why" for non-obvious library usage or architectural choices
91	- When choosing a new library or significant architectural approach, create a short decision record in `docs/decisions/NNN-title.md` explaining what was chosen and why
92	
93	## Documentation Maintenance
94	
95	When making changes that affect user-facing behavior, project structure, or available commands, check whether the following docs need updating:
96	
97	- `README.md` — UI description, available scripts, prerequisites, project documentation links
98	- `CLAUDE.md` — Architecture section, directory layout, commands, key patterns
99	- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Component hierarchy and technical details
100	- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — Project structure section, code guidelines
101	
102	If a PR adds a new panel, artifact type, API route, script, or dependency, update the relevant docs in the same PR.
103	
104	## PR Preparation
105	
106	- Generate detailed PR descriptions including: summary of changes, motivation/context, how to test, and areas of uncertainty or risk
107	- Flag sections where you used unfamiliar libraries or patterns that the reviewer should scrutinize
108	- Note which tests (if any) cover which functionality
109	- Keep PRs to one reviewable concept; prefer multiple smaller PRs over one large one

## Reuse

**No pre-existing equivalent.** `/repo/app/lib/utils/` contains no env-detection or path-resolution helper (only export/parser/DOM utilities), and `grep -rn "VERCEL|tmpdir|os.tmpdir"` across `/repo/app`, `/repo/scripts`, `/repo/verifier` matches nothing outside the new file. The helper is genuinely new, not a re-implementation.

**No missed call sites.** `process.cwd()` now appears exactly once in the repo (`app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts:13`); `persist.ts` and `cache.ts` were the only two modules that had it. `verifier/server.ts` resolves paths from `__dirname` for a separate Express service with its own deploy layout, and `scripts/*.mjs` take CLI-arg paths — neither belongs behind this helper. So the PR's conversion is complete.

## Candidates

1. **app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts:14** — `subpaths.length > 0 ? join(base, ...subpaths) : base` is a dead branch; `join(base)` with zero extra args already returns `base` (both `base` forms are already normalized). *failure_scenario:* an extra conditional a future reader has to reason about ("is there a case where join mangles the base?") and an untestable branch — either arm can be deleted with no behavior change, so the ternary is pure maintenance cost. `return join(base, ...subpaths);` is equivalent.

2. **app/lib/llm/cache.ts:27-32 and app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:11-15** — two different "make sure the data dir exists" implementations (async memoized `mkdir` vs. sync `existsSync`/`mkdirSync`) survive the refactor while the path logic was centralized. *failure_scenario:* the helper unified *where* to write but not *how to create it*, so any future change (permissions/mode, error swallowing on read-only FS, a third consumer) has to be made twice in two idioms. An `ensureDataDir(...subpaths)` in `dataDir.ts` returning the created path would leave both callers with zero fs boilerplate.

3. **app/lib/llm/cache.ts:27** — `let dirEnsured = false` is redundant module state guarding an already-idempotent `mkdir(..., { recursive: true })`. *failure_scenario:* a module-global that must be reset between tests and can go stale (dir deleted externally, or `/tmp` wiped between warm invocations on Vercel — exactly the environment this PR is adding support for) leaves `dirEnsured === true` while the dir is gone, and the guard saves only a sub-millisecond syscall on a path that already does file I/O.

4. **app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:6-7** — comment points at a "Deploy to Vercel" README section that does not exist (`grep -rni vercel /repo/README.md /repo/docs /repo/CLAUDE.md` → no matches) and otherwise restates the JSDoc it explicitly defers to. *failure_scenario:* a dangling cross-reference sends the next reader hunting through docs for nothing, and the duplicated rationale now has two places to drift out of sync with `dataDir()`'s own docblock.

- **Invariant removed:** the old `join(process.cwd(), "data")` meant build-time and request-time resolved to the same durable file, so a stale prerender was at least eventually consistent with a checked-in/volume-mounted `data/`.
- **Failure scenario:** on Vercel, `next build` runs with `VERCEL=1` set, so `readAnalyticsEntries()` executes at build against `/tmp/analytics.jsonl` (empty), and `{"entries":[]}` is baked into the static output. `useAnalytics.ts:11` then fetches that frozen empty payload forever. The diff makes writes succeed on Vercel while reads still never reflect them — the stated goal of the change is not achieved end-to-end.

**2. `app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:8` + `app/api/analytics/route.ts:10` — per-container `/tmp` shards analytics and makes `DELETE` partial**

- **Invariant removed:** `<cwd>/data/analytics.jsonl` was a single file shared by every request in the process/host, so `appendAnalyticsEntry` and `clearAnalyticsEntries` operated on one authoritative log.
- **Failure scenario:** on Vercel each concurrent Function instance has its own `/tmp`. N warm containers produce N disjoint `analytics.jsonl` files. `GET /api/analytics` returns whichever shard its container holds, and `DELETE` (`clearAnalyticsEntries`) truncates only that one shard — the user clicks "clear", the UI refetches, and older entries reappear from a sibling container. Cost totals shown in the dashboard are a random fraction of real spend. The new comment only warns about cold starts, not about sharding.

**3. `app/lib/llm/cache.ts:27-32` — the `dirEnsured` memo's correctness depended on the directory being durable**

```ts
let dirEnsured = false;
async function ensureCacheDir() {
  if (dirEnsured) return;
  await mkdir(CACHE_DIR, { recursive: true });
  dirEnsured = true;
}
```

- **Invariant removed:** with `CACHE_DIR = <cwd>/data/cache`, once created the directory persisted for the module's entire lifetime, so caching the "already ensured" flag at module scope was safe.
- **Failure scenario:** `CACHE_DIR` is now `/tmp/cache`, whose lifetime is not tied to the module instance — Vercel can reclaim `/tmp` contents under disk pressure while the container (and therefore `dirEnsured === true`) stays warm. `ensureCacheDir()` then short-circuits, and every subsequent `setCachedResult` rejects with `ENOENT`. Because `callLlm.ts:94` and `streamLlm.ts:64` swallow cache-write errors, the app silently degrades to 0% cache hit rate and pays full LLM cost on every call, with no log line. The findings cluster around the Vercel target itself — the most significant being that per-instance `/tmp` makes the analytics API incoherent there (arbitrary shards on read, partial clears on delete), which the new comment doesn't acknowledge, plus a comment pointing at a "Deploy to Vercel" README section that was never written.

Candidates I investigated and rejected during verification, so you know they were considered:

- **"GET /api/analytics is statically prerendered and baked empty at build"** — refuted. This repo runs Next.js 16.2.4, and since Next 15 GET route handlers are dynamic by default, so reads hit runtime `/tmp` as intended.
- **"`dirEnsured` memo goes stale if Vercel reclaims `/tmp` mid-life"** — dropped. Vercel preserves `/tmp` for the container's lifetime, and that code is unchanged from main.
- Unbounded cache growth against Vercel's 512 MB `/tmp` and pre-existing issues surfaced along the way (the swallowed-`cacheKey` eviction gap in `callLlm.ts`, the stale-UI guard in `useAnalytics.ts`) — real but either speculative in severity or outside this diff, so not reported as findings.
